title: A kimi-k3 experiment service runs B300 tasks end to end; twelve of thirteen campaigns are protocol-adherent, and the refused one used a tool the authoring environment does not offer

evidence.note: One workspace per task, each holding its own study.json, campaign-lock.json, campaign-evidence hash chain and report.json. The sweep ledger sweep-20260916-034037.tsv records each task's exit code and workspace.

observation:
Seven tasks ran through tools/launch_task.py on B300 with kimi-k3 as the authoring provider, reached over an Anthropic-compatible endpoint the repository owner supplied. All seven campaigns report campaign_complete, archive_integrity, filesystem_custody_verified and semantic_replay true, and every run is protocol_adherence 'adhered' with endpoint_observation 'qualified'. Five terminated at maximum_turns and two at the provider token limit. Measured candidate and baseline logical task bandwidth, as reference percentages: rmsnorm 5.79/5.48 against 5.11/5.07; layernorm 5.36/5.36 against 3.65; softmax 5.32 against 5.25; silu 6.21 against 5.39; swiglu 6.08 and 4.33 against 5.59/5.44; gelu_tanh 3.01 against 2.97; residual_rmsnorm 8.21 and 6.10 against 6.10/6.04. Best confirmed latencies ranged 0.0021 to 0.0044 ms. Token spend per campaign ranged 130577 to 283531.

Two environment facts cost a campaign before these ran. The launcher's default gpu-run socket is /tmp/agent-gpu-broker.sock and this host's broker listens on /tmp/h210fix-gpu.sock, so the first attempt reached the allocator and faulted with 'cannot reach broker' after the provider had already authored and sealed a candidate -- 77103 tokens spent on a run that could not be evaluated. The second is that node and Claude Code are installed under ~/.local/bin on this host and are not on a non-login shell's PATH, and the host has no route to the public internet, so neither is installable at run time.

A second sweep over the optimizer and row-wise families adds six more: momentum_sgd 9.31 candidate against 9.31/9.27 baseline, adamw 17.70 and 11.47 against 11.29, adadelta 11.20 against 11.03, softmax_backward 7.59/7.59 against 6.68/6.68, rmsnorm_input_gradient 8.11/7.34 against 6.70/6.49. Five of the six are adhered and qualified like the first seven.

The sixth is the interesting one. `bias_gradient_reduction` terminated at four events with protocol_adherence 'provider_fault' and the message 'Claude tool invocation differs'. Its retained transcript shows why: the authoring turn invoked Bash, Glob, Write and StructuredOutput, and the authoring environment offers Read, Write, Edit, Glob and Grep -- the CLI is launched with `--tools` and `--allowedTools` naming exactly those, and CLAUDE_AUTHORING_TOOLS is checked again on every returned block. So a model reached through this endpoint emitted a tool_use for a tool it was not offered, and the gate refused the run rather than accepting an authoring environment that differs from the other twelve. This is the same class as F-2026-09-13-003's protocol repairs, arriving from a different model: what the CLI passes as an allowed-tool list is not necessarily what a non-Anthropic endpoint honours, and only the harness's own re-check caught it.
proposed_change:
No Compiler or Executor change is proposed. What this establishes is that the artifact-optimization path works end to end under a non-Anthropic model reached through an Anthropic-compatible endpoint, which was previously only exercised with Claude and Kimi builds recorded in F-2026-09-13-003. Claim scope is artifact_optimization_only and estimand_available is false on every run, so these are not arm comparisons and none of the ratios above is a speedup claim against an external reference; they are candidate-versus-baseline measurements inside one task, case, target and assay.

The broker-socket default is worth routing: a launcher that defaults to a socket path this host does not use spends a full authoring turn before finding out. Either the default is discovered from the running broker, or the launcher probes the socket before it admits the provider -- the second is cheaper and refuses before any token is spent.

The Bash invocation is worth watching rather than acting on yet: one occurrence in thirteen campaigns is not evidence for a rule (AGENTS.md, 'a one-off failure is not evidence for a rule'). What it does establish is that the second check -- re-validating every returned tool_use against CLAUDE_AUTHORING_TOOLS rather than trusting the CLI's --allowedTools -- is load-bearing for a non-Anthropic endpoint, and should not be removed as redundant.
verification_plan: Behavior finding, so verification is by campaign. The seven workspaces above are the observation; a second sweep over the optimizer, row-wise and reduction families on the same Executor and Compiler Revisions tests whether adherence and qualification hold across task shapes rather than only the normalization and activation families.
